subject: Private deployment addendum — license scope, key custody & audit coordination
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@orchidbio.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Wu <emily.wu@orchidbio.com>, Orchid Legal <legal@orchidbio.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment requirements and licensing questions

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the throughput numbers look promising for our imaging inference workloads. Before we move onto a PO, our legal and security teams asked for clarification on a few private deployment items so we can scope the internal procurement review. Can you confirm the following:

- License scope: does Redwood grant Orchid a perpetual on-prem license for the model weights or an inference-only license tied to our subscription?
- Key custody: we need to understand options for customer-managed KMS/HSM vs. Redwood custodied keys. Orchid prefers to retain control of encryption keys where PHI is involved.
- Audit rights: our compliance team requires the ability to perform an annual on-site or vendor-led audit that looks at deployment config, logs, and pipeline access. What level of audit access can Redwood commit to for a Private deployment?
- Escrow-like request: Orchid has asked whether model weights or a 'fallback image' can be placed in escrow if Redwood were to cease service. Is there an equivalent offering?

I've attached a short doc with our minimum technical/contractual asks (Orchid_requirements.docx). Please loop in your legal and product folks and let us know what is feasible. If easier, we can schedule a 30-min legal+security call later this week.

Thanks,
Tom Reyes
Head of Platform Engineering
Orchid Biotech

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@orchidbio.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment requirements and licensing questions

Tom — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. Looping Neha from legal so we can get ahead of the contract side. Quick answers for triage:

- License scope: our standard Private deployment is a time-limited inference license tied to the Order Form; we can discuss a limited perpetual fallback for specific scenarios but that is non-standard and needs commercial approval.
- Key custody: we strongly recommend customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for PHI workloads; Redwood can support both customer KMS and Redwood-managed keys but we prefer not to hold custody for PHI.
- Audit rights: we support vendor-led audits and can provide deployment logs, config exports, and remote evidence packages. On-site audits are negotiable; we typically limit scope to systems that store or process customer data.
- Escrow-like: we do not typically escrow full model weights. Alternatives we offer: (1) restricted key escrow (crypto metadata) under mutual NDA; (2) a sealed 'fallback image' held with a neutral custodian for extreme situations — requires separate MSA addendum.

I'll get a draft Private Deploy Addendum (attached) to show proposed language and suggested limits. Can you do a 30-min sync Thursday 10–11am PT?

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment requirements and licensing questions — internal legal notes

Vivek — quick read of Orchid's asks and my notes below (attaching internal_legal_notes.pdf). High-level suggestions before we respond formally:

1) License scope: propose language: "Customer is granted a non-exclusive, limited term license to use Redwood models for inference in the Customer environment for the Term of the Order Form; derivative rights and redistribution are expressly excluded." Offer a 12–24 month renewal path rather than perpetual transfer of weights.

2) Key custody: accept customer-managed KMS by default; if customer insists Redwood-managed keys, require contractual constraints (no export, access logs, monthly attestation).

3) Audit: narrow to "reasonable" audit rights, remote-first. For on-site audits, require 30 days' notice, scope limited to Redwood-hosted components that process Customer Data, and allow Redwood to redact trade-secret material. Offer SOC 2 reports and a vendor evidence package as primary deliverable.

4) Escrow-like: avoid escrow of model weights. Counterproposal: agree to escrow only to the extent of configuration artifacts and encrypted key material (wrapped keys) with a neutral custodian, released only on specified triggers (bankruptcy, cessation of service) after mutual confirmation and court scrutiny.

Recommend we send Orchid a redline of the Private Deploy Addendum with the above and propose an exec/legal 30-min call to resolve the last-mile items.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@orchidbio.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed Private Deployment Addendum and next steps

Tom — attaching our proposed draft addendum (RI_PrivateDeploy_Addendum_draft_v1.docx). High level:

- License: inference-only license tied to Order Form term; renewal path documented.
- Keys: customer-managed KMS preferred; Redwood-managed keys allowed with controls and monthly attestation.
- Audit: primary deliverable is SOC 2 + evidence package + remote logs; on-site audit by exception and limited scope.
- Escrow alternative: propose encrypted key-material escrow with neutral custodian (release triggers limited and described).

Action items from our side: Neha will prepare redline language for §§3.1 (License), 7.2 (Audit), and 9.4 (Escrow/Termination). From Orchid: please review the draft and send any redlines or markups.

Proposed times for a short legal+security call: Thu 13 May 10:00–10:30 PT or Fri 14 May 08:00–08:30 PT. Let me know which works and I'll send the invite.

Thanks,
Vivek
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: RI_PrivateDeploy_Addendum_draft_v1.docx

From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@orchidbio.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Orchid Legal <legal@orchidbio.com>, Emily Wu <emily.wu@orchidbio.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed Private Deployment Addendum and next steps

Vivek — thanks for the draft. We've reviewed and attached our redlines (Orchid_MSA_redlines.docx). A few points where Orchid is firm:

- Audit: Orchid requires contractual audit rights at least once per year, including the ability to bring a third-party auditor to review deployment configuration, logs, and controls relevant to our data. Remote review/signed SOC2 is helpful but not sufficient for our enterprise compliance.
- Escrow: Orchid expects model weights or a runnable fallback image to be placed with an independent escrow agent and released to Orchid if Redwood ceases to provide the service.

We appreciate the alternative escrow/key-material compromise, but the compliance team considers that insufficient without clear access to a runnable fallback.

We are available for the Thu 13 May 10am PT slot — happy to discuss and find a workable middle ground.

Regards,
Tom Reyes
Head of Platform Engineering
Orchid Biotech

Attachment: Orchid_MSA_redlines.docx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@orchidbio.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed Private Deployment Addendum and next steps — compromise proposal

Tom — appreciate the clear redlines. We want to keep this moving and avoid heavy legal delay. Proposed compromise we can take to execs:

1) Audit: agree to annual audit but limit to vendor-led or third-party auditor under a scoped, mutually agreed Statement of Work (max 3 days on-site; customer bears reasonable travel costs). Provide our SOC 2 report and full evidence package in advance and let the third-party auditor validate only the items in the SOW.

2) Escrow: we cannot routinely escrow full model weights. As an alternative Redwood will: (a) place a sealed, encrypted fallback image with a neutral custodian that contains only the runtime artifacts necessary to run inference (no proprietary training data or internal toolchain), (b) escrow wrapped key-material (customer-wrapped keys) and release only on specific triggers (insolvency, failure to maintain SLAs for X consecutive days), and (c) include a mutual attestation and release governance process. This is effectively a functional escrow with strong release controls.

3) License: keep inference-only license for the Order Form term with an express transition plan for data retention and cutoff. If Orchid requires a perpetual transfer in narrow situations (e.g., bankruptcy), we can include a narrowly-scoped carveout tied to the escrow release.

If that sounds workable I'll send a revised redline and a DocuSign link to proceed with the limited addendum + SOW acceptance. Also propose a 30-min legal call Monday to finalize SOW scope.

DocuSign (preliminary): https://www.docusign.com/Signing/?s=example-sign-link
Drive (evidence package): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRIOrchidAddendum

Best,
Vivek
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
